item.title: Reflecting on Python's Event Loop and sys.audit
item.description:
Note: I originally published a deep technical dive on this topic for the Fever Engineering blog. You can read the full article on Medium .

The “Why” Behind the Code

If you work with Python’s asyncio at scale, you know the specific kind of anxiety that comes with “random” latency spikes. We faced random 200ms freezes that left absolutely no trace in the logs.

At first, we had a simple log that would detect “slow” tasks, but we had no idea why they were slow. We had no stack trace, and looking for the issue in a massive codebase felt impossible.

item.title: Heavy Lifting: The Physics of Discipline
item.description:
Before I was optimizing backend latency, I was optimizing leverage.

For years, I’ve competed in powerlifting, reaching national-level numbers and having the opportunity to compete against the best in the country.

At first glance, moving heavy circles seems to have nothing to do with writing software. But if you ask me, the overlap is massive.

Competing at a high level requires a specific type of discipline—one that doesn’t just stay in the gym, but bleeds into every other aspect of your life. Surprisingly, lifting and coding share the same source code.
